boundary: Scores are dated KINGDOM prioritization judgments, not vendor rankings, procurement approval, scientific proof, partnership authority, or permission to use a provider. Revalidate volatile capabilities, versions, prices, regions, terms, standards, and security status before action.

score_guide.value_now: 0 has no present scoped value; 5 can create durable value now without requiring speculative advantage.
score_guide.openness: 0 is inaccessible or inseparable from one provider; 5 has open specifications or implementations and credible exit paths.
score_guide.lock_in_risk: 0 has negligible coupling; 5 creates substantial technical, commercial, data, or governance dependence. Higher is worse.

ecosystems.name: OpenQASM 3
ecosystems.valuable_capability: A human-readable circuit and hardware-description interchange with classical control and timing concepts.
ecosystems.power_boundary: Implementations may support only subsets, and accepted programs can still compile differently for each target.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Preserve validated OpenQASM exports beside the canonical problem and lossless native sidecars.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: OpenQASM portability does not mean identical performance or feature support on every backend.

ecosystems.name: Quantum Intermediate Representation Alliance
ecosystems.valuable_capability: An LLVM-based interchange for heterogeneous classical-quantum compilation with explicit profiles.
ecosystems.power_boundary: A QIR version, profile, target quantum instruction set, and runtime contract are all needed; QIR is not a universal binary.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Build conformance fixtures, round-trip tests, profile declarations, and readable evidence around QIR exports.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: QIR conformance does not prove that a target preserves every source-level semantic or hardware capability.

ecosystems.name: Qiskit and IBM Quantum Compute Service
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Mature circuit construction, transpilation, primitives, simulators, error work, and chemistry tooling.
ecosystems.power_boundary: The open SDK and abstract primitives are distinct from IBM-managed execution and server-side features.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Make Qiskit a first-class optional adapter while preserving circuits, observables, samples, passes, and mitigation settings outside IBM services.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: A result produced with a Qiskit or IBM mitigation workflow is not automatically portable or independently reproducible.

ecosystems.name: Cirq, qsim, and OpenFermion
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Strong circuit transformation, noise simulation, virtual-engine testing, and fermionic or chemistry representations.
ecosystems.power_boundary: Google hardware access is restricted and device-specific features create affinity even when the software is open.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Use Cirq and qsim as an independent simulator lane and OpenFermion as a chemistry interchange layer.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: A Google-style virtual device is not access to, or evidence from, a physical Google processor.

ecosystems.name: PennyLane and Catalyst
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Portable differentiable workflows, broad device plugins, and compiled hybrid quantum-classical programs.
ecosystems.power_boundary: Device plugins, gradient semantics, supported control flow, and compiler support vary; Catalyst remains under active development.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Use it as the rapid research frontend when gradients matter while keeping experiment semantics outside QNodes.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: One source program does not guarantee equivalent gradients, cost, or execution semantics across plugins.

ecosystems.name: NVIDIA CUDA-Q
ecosystems.valuable_capability: A CPU, GPU, and QPU programming model with scalable simulation, dynamics, error-correction work, and hardware backends.
ecosystems.power_boundary: The open toolchain still gains its strongest operational advantage from NVIDIA CUDA infrastructure and follows its compiler model.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Add after the portable local core, when a scoped Linux NVIDIA or HPC node exists; treat macOS execution as CPU-side only.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: Open source does not eliminate hardware, compiler, or roadmap affinity.

ecosystems.name: Amazon Braket
ecosystems.valuable_capability: One public route to several gate and neutral-atom QPUs plus local and managed simulators.
ecosystems.power_boundary: IAM, regions, S3, job containers, metrics, billing, and third-party hardware processing create multiple control and data boundaries.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Use as the first optional multi-hardware bridge only after cost, region, credential, payload-minimization, retry, and cancellation gates exist.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: A broker normalizes procurement, not hardware semantics, privacy terms, or comparative performance.

ecosystems.name: Microsoft QDK, resource estimator, and Azure Quantum
ecosystems.valuable_capability: A local fault-tolerant resource estimator, QIR tooling, Q#, and access to several provider families.
ecosystems.power_boundary: The estimator can be used locally, while Azure workspaces, storage, provider availability, and billing create cloud coupling.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Adopt the local estimator early and require physical-qubit, runtime, error-budget, and assumption fields for future-facing proposals.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: A resource estimate is not a roadmap promise or evidence that required hardware exists.

ecosystems.name: Quantinuum and pytket
ecosystems.valuable_capability: A strong compiler and backend abstraction plus advanced trapped-ion, emulator, adaptive-control, and QIR workflows.
ecosystems.power_boundary: Advanced control can be lost through a lowest-common-denominator frontend; Nexus, Guppy, and native behavior add affinity.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Use for adaptive and QIR comparison work, preserving both portable and exact native artifacts.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: Successful conversion from another SDK does not prove preservation of every dynamic or native capability.

ecosystems.name: IonQ
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Direct and brokered access with maintained routes from Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane, and CUDA-Q, plus abstract and native gates.
ecosystems.power_boundary: Provider compilation hides transformations while native gates improve control at the cost of device-family coupling.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Use as one trapped-ion comparison target and record client versus provider compilation and compiled gate counts.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: Raw qubit counts or abstract-circuit similarity do not make cross-provider results comparable.

ecosystems.name: QuEra Bloqade and Pasqal Pulser
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Programmable geometries and analog Hamiltonian experiments suited to lattice, spin, many-body, and materials questions.
ecosystems.power_boundary: Analog programs are not faithfully reducible to ordinary gate circuits, and early APIs can be unstable.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Create a separate analog-Hamiltonian execution family instead of forcing these systems through a gate adapter.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: Fit between a hardware Hamiltonian and a scientific model does not make the device a generic accelerator.

ecosystems.name: D-Wave Ocean and Leap
ecosystems.valuable_capability: A developed stack for binary, constrained, nonlinear, classical, annealing, and hybrid optimization workflows.
ecosystems.power_boundary: The problem model and execution paradigm are not interchangeable with gate-model QAOA; managed hybrid internals obscure quantum contribution.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Maintain a distinct optimization family with exact, MIP, local-search, and heuristic baselines under the same problem contract.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: A managed hybrid solver win does not establish that its quantum component caused the gain.

ecosystems.name: UK NQCC SparQ Access
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Assured multi-platform access, application discovery, skills, and UK quantum-readiness routes without immediate hardware procurement.
ecosystems.power_boundary: Access is eligibility-, allocation-, programme-, and timeframe-dependent; applications and partnerships require separate authority.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Prepare a credible benchmark and evidence package locally, then consider an industry expression of interest only with explicit approval.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: Programme availability does not guarantee allocation, suitability, continuity, or free production compute.

ecosystems.name: NIST post-quantum standards and migration programme
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Final ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA standards plus migration, KEM, inventory, interoperability, and crypto-agility guidance.
ecosystems.power_boundary: Standards still require maintained implementations, pinned revisions and errata, protocol integration, testing, rotation, and operational governance.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Begin a no-key-material cryptographic census and crypto-agility design now; never implement a new KINGDOM primitive.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: A standardized algorithm is not automatically a secure implementation, validated module, protocol, or deployment.

ecosystems.name: OpenSSL 3.5 LTS and IETF PQC protocol standards
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Native standardized PQC plus standards-track hybrid TLS key agreement and ML-DSA formats for X.509, JOSE, and COSE.
ecosystems.power_boundary: Hybrid key agreement is not hybrid authentication, a patched release is required, and native support is not the same as FIPS 140 validation.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Build controlled interoperability canaries that record negotiated suites, fallback, fragmentation, versions, and separate authentication properties.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: Successful negotiation does not establish endpoint, certificate, identity, application, or regulated-deployment security.

ecosystems.name: Open Quantum Safe
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Cross-implementation testing, candidate evaluation, test vectors, fuzzing, and protocol prototyping.
ecosystems.power_boundary: The project describes its integrations as research and not production quality; standardized algorithms should use maintained native providers where available.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Confine OQS to an isolated interoperability lab with minimal builds and explicit non-production labels.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: Availability through liboqs or oqs-provider does not establish production readiness or standards status.

ecosystems.name: SeQUeNCe quantum-network simulator
ecosystems.valuable_capability: An open discrete-event simulator spanning hardware, entanglement, resource, network, and application layers.
ecosystems.power_boundary: Simulation assumptions and scheduler policy can dominate results; a simulated network is not a deployed quantum link.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Use as the first backend-neutral networking sandbox and cross-check material claims in a second implementation.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: A simulator result does not establish hardware feasibility, security, deployment, or useful network capacity.

ecosystems.name: NetQASM, SquidASM, NetSquid, and QNodeOS research stack
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Influential application-ISA, simulation, and node-operating-system concepts for programmable quantum networks.
ecosystems.power_boundary: NetQASM cites patent and commercial-licensing requirements, SquidASM depends on account-gated NetSquid, and QNodeOS source is not open.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Study interfaces and reproduce concepts in open fixtures without making the stack an undeclared dependency.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: A primary laboratory demonstration is not a generally available open operating system or network service.

ecosystems.name: Quantum key distribution
ecosystems.valuable_capability: Specialized physical-layer key-distribution research under narrow assumptions.
ecosystems.power_boundary: QKD does not authenticate its source, requires dedicated links and hardware, adds relay and implementation risk, and does not secure endpoints or stored data.
ecosystems.kingdom_move: Do not procure it as a defensive capability; admit only labelled, non-production research with ordinary post-quantum authentication.
ecosystems.does_not_prove: QKD is not general encryption, identity, application security, endpoint protection, or a replacement for PQC.

modules.name: Quantum Experiment Bundle
modules.does: Keeps a canonical problem, falsifiable hypothesis, baseline, metrics, rights, budget, stop rule, and artifact references together.
modules.does_not: It does not approve a provider run or establish scientific truth.

modules.name: Capability Registry
modules.does: Records dated capabilities, openness, lock-in, regions, limits, profiles, and source evidence.
modules.does_not: It does not guarantee live availability, pricing, suitability, or vendor claims.

modules.name: Simulator Matrix
modules.does: Runs local reference and, later, independent framework simulations against shared fixtures.
modules.does_not: It does not turn simulator output into hardware evidence.

modules.name: Standards Bridge
modules.does: Exports and validates OpenQASM and QIR with profile, loss, and native-sidecar receipts.
modules.does_not: It does not pretend that analog, annealing, pulse, and gate programs are interchangeable.

modules.name: Provider Access Broker
modules.does: Will enforce simulator-first routing, credential scope, data and region policy, price ceilings, cancellation, and no automatic retry.
modules.does_not: It does not grant credentials, credits, spending, or provider authority.

modules.name: Quantum Receipt Ledger
modules.does: Binds sources, versions, compilation, target, shots, results, baseline, cost, and limitations to a dated evidence grade.
modules.does_not: It does not create truth, identity, consent, reputation, reward, or on-chain finality.

modules.name: Advantage Claim Gate
modules.does: Maps evidence from E0 through E5 and reserves practical-advantage language for robust operational evidence.
modules.does_not: It does not make a benchmark fair merely by labelling it.

modules.name: Chemistry and Materials Forge
modules.does: Will compare active-space, Hamiltonian, sampling, embedding, mitigation, and resource-estimation workflows.
modules.does_not: It does not promise commercial chemistry advantage from present QPUs.

modules.name: Optimization Arena
modules.does: Will compare exact, MIP, local-search, heuristic, annealing, gate, and justified analog mappings under one problem contract.
modules.does_not: It does not attribute a managed hybrid result to a hidden quantum component.

modules.name: Fault-Tolerant Observatory
modules.does: Will compare logical and physical resource estimates across explicit error-correction and hardware assumptions.
modules.does_not: It does not convert an estimate into a vendor roadmap or delivery date.

modules.name: Quantum Learning Commons
modules.does: Creates tutorials, fixtures, contribution paths, reviewer credit, and independent reproductions.
modules.does_not: It does not turn credentials or expertise into unchallengeable jurisdiction.

modules.name: Cryptographic Census
modules.does: Inventories algorithms, protocols, trust roots, dependencies, lifetimes, owners, and migration targets without key material.
modules.does_not: It does not read, store, rotate, or revoke keys.

modules.name: Algorithm Policy Boundary
modules.does: Separates KEM, signature, AEAD, and hashing policy; pins reviewed suites; prevents downgrade; records expiring exceptions.
modules.does_not: It does not invent algorithms or keep every legacy option enabled in the name of agility.

modules.name: Hybrid Transport Lab
modules.does: Will test standards-track hybrid TLS in a controlled canary and measure negotiation, fallback, size, latency, and interoperability.
modules.does_not: It does not treat PQ key agreement as PQ authentication or production approval.

modules.name: Long-Lived Proof Transition
modules.does: Tests explicit all-required traditional and post-quantum proof sets, rotation, revocation, and historical verification.
modules.does_not: It does not infer personhood, consciousness, continuity, consent, or authority from a signature.

modules.name: Ledger Quantum-Readiness Lab
modules.does: Benchmarks signature size, verification, throughput, state growth, gossip, rotation, recovery, and legacy exposure before any Zerone design choice.
modules.does_not: It does not call Zerone quantum-safe or modify consensus.

modules.name: Quantum Network Commons
modules.does: Models entanglement requests, classical control, topology, fidelity, latency, expiry, failure, and reproducibility in open simulators.
modules.does_not: It does not claim a deployed quantum network or production security.

modules.name: Entanglement Allocation Governance
modules.does: Makes scarce-resource priority, allocation, wait, preemption, failure, consumption, and appeal legible.
modules.does_not: It does not let money, status, or institutional prestige silently become scheduler priority.

power_centers.leverage: Accounts, regions, credentials, queues, billing, storage, logs, and provider routing.
power_centers.risk: Spend, data, retry, and availability become opaque or hard to exit.
power_centers.counterweight: Local-first execution, minimized payloads, explicit price and retry caps, exportable artifacts, and a second route.
power_centers.hold_authority: A separate budget and data steward can stop external execution.

power_centers.leverage: Native gates, topology, calibration, pulse access, emulators, roadmaps, and result interpretation.
power_centers.risk: Marketing metrics or native capabilities define the question and comparison.
power_centers.counterweight: Canonical problems, raw and compiled artifact retention, calibration receipts, modality comparison, and exit tests.
power_centers.hold_authority: An independent reproduction reviewer can hold promotion.

power_centers.leverage: APIs, defaults, deprecations, transformations, gradients, and supported backends.
power_centers.risk: Invisible compiler or API changes alter results or make an ecosystem indispensable.
power_centers.counterweight: Version pins, conformance fixtures, semantic receipts, native sidecars, and multiple implementations.
power_centers.hold_authority: The capability gate rejects unreviewed version or semantic changes.

power_centers.leverage: The interchange vocabulary, profiles, identifiers, and compatibility rules.
power_centers.risk: Nominal openness hides incomplete profiles, patent terms, or implementer asymmetry.
power_centers.counterweight: Public issue participation, licence and patent review, reference tests, and explicit unsupported features.
power_centers.hold_authority: Legal and technical review can keep a standard out of a release profile.

power_centers.controller: Problem, dataset, metric, and comparison designers
power_centers.leverage: They define what counts as success and which classical work is visible.
power_centers.risk: Cherry-picking, parameter fishing, weak baselines, and hidden preprocessing manufacture advantage.
power_centers.counterweight: Preregistration, strong baseline review, total-cost accounting, negative results, and independent replication.
power_centers.hold_authority: A baseline reviewer independent of the implementer can refuse the claim grade.

power_centers.controller: Grant makers, investors, vendors, and programme sponsors
power_centers.leverage: Access, time, visibility, salaries, equipment, and the problem agenda.
power_centers.risk: Funding converts into suppressed negatives, inflated claims, or governance influence.
power_centers.counterweight: Conflict disclosure, sponsor-independent release review, diversified support, and a mission-fit stop rule.
power_centers.hold_authority: The rights and release steward can stop sponsor-shaped publication.

power_centers.controller: Researchers, reviewers, educators, and credentialing institutions
power_centers.leverage: Interpretation, language, access, status, and qualification.
power_centers.risk: Expertise becomes jurisdiction or a priesthood that cannot be challenged.
power_centers.counterweight: Plain-language curricula, reproducible fixtures, dissent, appeal, documented uncertainty, and reviewer rotation.
power_centers.hold_authority: A rights-aware appeal path can challenge expertise without retaliation.

power_centers.controller: Holders of scientific, commercial, personal, or operational data
power_centers.leverage: They determine which questions can be tested and which payloads can leave a boundary.
power_centers.risk: Sensitive data is exposed through circuits, parameters, logs, provider retention, or immutable receipts.
power_centers.counterweight: Synthetic-first work, data minimization, local preprocessing, classification, retention limits, and digest-only evidence.
power_centers.hold_authority: The data steward can veto export regardless of scientific value.

power_centers.controller: Validators, maintainers, treasury, token holders, and bridge operators
power_centers.leverage: They can convert receipts into permanence, rewards, qualification, or economic weight.
power_centers.risk: Spectacular claims become immutable, rewarded, or politically authoritative before reproduction.
power_centers.counterweight: Off-chain first, candidate-only projections, zero reward, challenge periods, corrections, replay protection, and separation of powers.
power_centers.hold_authority: No automatic Zerone projection; independent evidence and governance holds remain required.

power_centers.leverage: Priority, fidelity, deadlines, preemption, routing, and expiring scarce resources.
power_centers.risk: Money, status, or institutional prestige silently controls access and creates starvation.
power_centers.counterweight: Decision receipts, declared authority, fairness metrics, denial-of-service tests, cancellation, and appeal.
power_centers.hold_authority: A governance reviewer can freeze an allocation policy before any external deployment.
